quests.instruction: A heavy monsoon shower has started and Anu cannot go out to play. Which plan fits?
options: Fly a Kite in the Field 🪁
quests.hint: Consider what you can do while staying dry.
quests.explanation: Heavy rain makes roads slippery and fields muddy, so an indoor game keeps everyone dry and safe.
quests.funFact: The southwest monsoon usually reaches Kerala around the start of June.

quests.instruction: It is a very hot afternoon. Which plan is best for playing outside?
quests.correctAnswer: Play in the Shade with Water 🌳
options: Play in the Shade with Water 🌳
Run Races in the Midday Sun ☀️
quests.hint: Consider how to stay cool and not get too thirsty.
quests.explanation: Shade keeps the sun off, and water replaces what the body loses through sweat, so both help in the heat.
quests.funFact: Standing in shade can feel noticeably cooler than standing in direct sunshine.

quests.instruction: Thunder rumbles and lightning flashes while Dev is at home. Where should he stay?
options: In the Middle of a Field 🌾
quests.hint: Remember where lightning cannot easily reach you.
quests.explanation: A building gives protection, and keeping away from windows lowers the chance of being hurt if glass breaks. Tall trees and open fields are risky places in a storm.
quests.funFact: Lightning is hotter than the surface of the Sun, which is why it can be so dangerous.

quests.instruction: Which of these is a job done most days?
quests.hint: Consider what comes round again every morning.
quests.explanation: Making the bed happens daily for many people. A dentist visit or a haircut only happens now and then.
quests.funFact: Calendar apps often let you set a task to repeat every day, week or month.

quests.instruction: Which of these is usually done about once a week or every two weeks?
quests.hint: Focus on a job that does not need doing every day but still comes back.
quests.explanation: Sheets collect dust and sweat, so they are changed and washed regularly, often every week or two. Brushing hair and eating lunch happen daily.
quests.funFact: Dust mites, tiny creatures too small to see, live in bedding, and regular washing helps keep their numbers down.

quests.instruction: Which of these happens only a couple of times a year?
quests.hint: The key is a check-up that is booked ahead rather than done daily.
quests.explanation: A dentist visit happens a couple of times a year, which makes it an occasional routine and not a daily one.
quests.funFact: Dentists often suggest a check-up about every six months.

quests.instruction: Ravi is riding on a crowded bus. What is the safe thing to do?
quests.hint: Decide what keeps you steady if the bus brakes suddenly.
quests.explanation: Buses can brake or turn suddenly, so holding a rail or sitting down keeps you steady. Leaning out or standing by the door is dangerous.
quests.funFact: Buses in many cities have a bell or button so passengers can tell the driver when to stop.

quests.instruction: The family is about to set off in the car. What should each person do before it starts moving?
options: Hold Their Bags on Their Laps 🎒
quests.hint: Remember what keeps you in your seat if the car stops suddenly.
quests.explanation: A seat belt holds you in place if the car brakes suddenly, so it is fastened before the car begins to move.
quests.funFact: Children usually need a booster seat until they are tall enough for an adult seat belt to fit properly.

quests.instruction: On a long train journey, Mina's family wants to keep things safe. Which habit helps?
quests.hint: Think about how to avoid losing things and each other.
quests.explanation: Keeping bags close stops them being lost or tripped over, and staying with the group means nobody gets separated.
quests.funFact: Indian Railways carries millions of passengers every day.

quests.instruction: Zoya's grandparents arrive at the door. What is a kind way to greet them?
options: Hide in Her Room Until Later 🚪
quests.hint: Work out how you want visitors to feel when they arrive.
quests.explanation: A warm greeting makes guests feel welcome. Ignoring them or hiding can make them feel unwelcome.
quests.funFact: The Malayalam word 'swagatham' means welcome.

quests.instruction: A friend comes over to play with Ravi's toys. What helps the visit go well?
quests.hint: Think about how a guest should feel in your home.
quests.explanation: Sharing helps a friend enjoy the visit. Hiding toys or banning touching makes it less fun for both of them.
quests.funFact: Senet, one of the oldest known board games, was played in ancient Egypt more than 4,000 years ago.

quests.instruction: Maya borrowed a book from a friend. What should she do when she has finished it?
quests.hint: The clue is whose book it is.
quests.explanation: Returning a borrowed book on time shows respect for its owner, who may want to read it again.
quests.funFact: Libraries use due dates for the same reason, so other readers get a turn.

quests.instruction: Aman has a dentist appointment this morning. Which step makes sense before he leaves home?
quests.hint: Work out what the dentist will be looking at.
quests.explanation: Clean teeth make the check-up easier and more comfortable, so brushing before going is a thoughtful step.
quests.funFact: Dentists use a small mirror on a handle to see the backs of teeth.

quests.instruction: In the doctor's waiting room, children are waiting for their turn. Which behaviour fits?
quests.hint: Consider the other people who may feel unwell.
quests.explanation: Some people waiting may feel unwell, so quiet waiting is kind. Running or touching equipment can cause accidents.
quests.funFact: The stethoscope was invented in 1816 by a French doctor named René Laennec.

quests.instruction: Ira feels dizzy and sick during a lesson at school. What should she do?
options: Hide It and Keep On Going 🙈
quests.hint: Ask yourself who can help at school.
quests.explanation: A teacher can look after her or call a family member, so telling them early is the safest choice.
quests.funFact: Most schools keep a first-aid kit and have trained staff to help children who feel unwell.

quests.instruction: Aman often feels rushed in the mornings. Which routine would help most?
quests.hint: Ask yourself what could be done earlier, when there is no hurry.
quests.explanation: Doing jobs the evening before takes pressure off the morning. Waking later or skipping breakfast would make the rush worse.
quests.funFact: Making a short list of morning jobs can help children do them without reminders.

quests.instruction: Meera often loses her pencils. Which habit would help most?
quests.hint: Consider how you know where to look.
quests.explanation: When pencils go back to the same spot every time, she knows where to look and nothing gets lost.
quests.funFact: A pencil case keeps small items together so they do not slip to the bottom of a bag.

quests.instruction: The classroom floor is covered in scraps of paper by the end of the day. Which routine would help?
quests.hint: Think about what could be done a few minutes before everyone leaves.
quests.explanation: A short tidy-up before the bell means the room is clean when the day ends, and everyone shares the work.
quests.funFact: In Japan, many schoolchildren clean their classrooms together every day.

quests.instruction: Zoya's family is going to the market. Which bag helps cut down on plastic bags?
quests.hint: Focus on a bag that can be used many times.
quests.explanation: A cloth bag can be reused again and again, so fewer single-use plastic bags are needed.
quests.funFact: Some plastic bags can take hundreds of years to break down.

quests.instruction: At the museum, a guide is explaining an old object. What should the children do?
quests.hint: Consider how to learn the most while others listen too.
quests.explanation: Listening and asking questions helps children learn. Touching displays can damage them, and loud talking disturbs others.
quests.funFact: Museums often ask visitors not to touch old objects, because oils from hands can damage them.

quests.instruction: At the beach, Priya wants to swim. What should come first?
options: Swim Out Far on Her Own 🏊
quests.hint: The clue is who should know before anyone goes into the water.
quests.explanation: Water can be unpredictable, so a grown-up should know and be watching before children go in.
quests.funFact: On beaches in many countries, red and yellow flags mark the area patrolled by lifeguards.

quests.instruction: Before going to a neighbour's house to play, what should Aarav do?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell a Grown-up Where He Is Going 🗣️
options: Tell a Grown-up Where He Is Going 🗣️
Ask a Stranger to Walk with Him 🧍
quests.hint: Think about who should know where you are.
quests.explanation: Grown-ups need to know where a child is so they can find them and keep them safe.
quests.funFact: A phone number written on a card kept in the school bag helps a child who gets separated from a grown-up.

quests.instruction: A person Meera does not know offers her a ride home from school. What should she do?
quests.correctAnswer: Say No and Tell a Grown-up 🛑
options: Say Yes if They Seem Friendly 🙂
Take the Ride Just This Once 🚗
Say No and Tell a Grown-up 🛑
quests.hint: The clue is who is safe to go with.
quests.explanation: Children should only go with people their family has agreed on. Saying no and telling a trusted adult keeps her safe.
quests.funFact: Having at least two trusted adults to turn to means a child still has someone to ask if one is not around.

quests.instruction: Kabir smells smoke in the kitchen at home. What should he do?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell a Grown-up and Go Outside 🚪
options: Tell a Grown-up and Go Outside 🚪
Open the Fridge to Check It 🧊
Stay and Wait for a Grown-up to Find Him 🔍
quests.hint: Focus on getting away from the smoke and getting help.
quests.explanation: Smoke can be dangerous, so a child should tell a grown-up, leave the room and let the grown-up deal with it.
quests.funFact: In India, 112 is the number grown-ups can call in an emergency.

quests.instruction: Rohan has had half an hour of tablet time, which was the plan. What is the best next step?
quests.correctAnswer: Switch It Off and Do Something Else 📴
options: Start a Different Game on It 🎮
Ask for Another Hour of Tablet Time 🙏
Switch It Off and Do Something Else 📴
quests.hint: Work out what keeping to a plan means.
quests.explanation: Sticking to the agreed time shows self-control and leaves time for other things.
quests.funFact: Eye experts suggest looking at something about six metres away for 20 seconds after every 20 minutes of screen time.

quests.instruction: Dinner is called while Mina is in the middle of drawing. What is a good response?
quests.correctAnswer: Stop at a Good Place and Come 🍽️
options: Keep Drawing Until It Is Finished 🎨
Stop at a Good Place and Come 🍽️
Ask for Dinner to Be Kept for Hours ⏳
quests.hint: Focus on the people waiting at the table.
quests.explanation: Finishing the line you are on and then going shows respect for others. Making everyone wait is not fair.
quests.funFact: Artists often put a drawing aside and return to it later with fresh eyes.

quests.instruction: Mum says 'five more minutes' as the family plays in the park. What does it mean?
quests.correctAnswer: Time to Finish and Get Ready to Go ⏳
options: Time to Finish and Get Ready to Go ⏳
Stay for as Long as You Would Like 🏞️
Start a Brand New Game Instead 🎠
quests.hint: The clue is what a warning before leaving is for.
quests.explanation: A five-minute warning gives time to finish and get ready, so leaving does not come as a shock.
quests.funFact: A countdown, such as 'five more minutes', gives children time to finish what they are doing.

quests.instruction: Fastening a seat belt, holding the bus rail and telling a grown-up where you are going all belong to which group of habits?
quests.hint: Ask yourself what each of these protects.
quests.explanation: Each habit helps keep a child safe while out and about.
quests.funFact: High-visibility vests are worn near roads so that people can be seen easily.

quests.instruction: Greeting guests, sharing toys and returning a borrowed book show which kind of habits?
quests.hint: The clue is how each habit makes other people feel.
quests.explanation: Each of these shows care for other people, which is what kindness habits are about.
quests.funFact: Researchers have found that sharing and helping tend to make people feel happier.

quests.instruction: Switching off a screen on time, putting one game away before starting another, and waiting for your turn all show what?
quests.hint: The key is holding back from what you want right now.
quests.explanation: Each one means pausing what you feel like doing for something that matters more, which is self-control.
quests.funFact: Self-control tends to grow as children get older, and practising small habits helps.
